title: Food Safety Characteristics of Airline Catering: Analysis of Critical Points in the Technological Chain through the Practice of an International Catering Supply Base
content: Food safety management in airline catering is exceptionally vulnerable to temperature fluctuations and strict time-space displacement, as the isolated cabin environment limits any possibility for thermal or technological corrective actions during flight. Grounded in a comprehensive hazard analysis targeting microbiological pathogens (Salmonella spp., Listeria monocytogenes, vegetative bacterial cells) and physical/chemical risks, this study evaluates under what technological parameters food safety can be rigorously maintained across a high-volume international catering base. The methodology analyzed the HACCP system and PRPs by continuously monitoring thermal processing (CCP1: ≥74°C poultry, ≥65°C red meat and blast chilling (CCP2: 63°C to 10°C within 90 min), alongside raw material CPs ≤5°C, ≤-18°C frozen and an annual ATP monitoring program N=550, (Table 2 with 100% corrective re-test compliance). Continuous digital monitoring (Qoodo) and accredited microbiological testing (n=200) confirmed that strict adherence to these critical limits consistently prevented recontamination and maintained the 0- -5°C cold chain during transport using dry ice and high-loader vehicles. Aviation food safety depends on the integrated operation of the entire chain, offering a reference for other long-distance food transport systems.
